en: The reviewer is glad that, shortly after the appearance of the former volume, a new volume of Jacobi's collected works has appeared, and wishes the noble old man, as well as the public, good fortune in the undisturbed continuation of this enterprise. - The present third volume contains four writings which, in the words of the preface, "are to some extent also parts of a whole that arose simultaneously and have only fallen apart, a whole which repeats itself in each of these parts in a different way".
They are: 1. the letter of Jacobi to Fichte published in the year 1799; 2.
the essay which we read first in Reinhold's Beiträge etc., 31.
issue of 1801, 'On the enterprise of bringing criticism to bear on reason so as to reduce it to understanding, and of giving philosophy in general a new view'; 3.
'On a Prophecy of Lichtenberg', first printed in 1801; 4.
the treatise 'On the Divine Things and Their Revelation', with a preface to the present new edition.
An interesting addition of 23 letters to Johann
Müller, G[eorg] Forster, Herder, Kant (including one from Kant to Jacobi), Privy
Councillor Schlosser, J[ohann] G[eorg] Jacobi and to some unnamed persons closes the volume.
zh: 书评者对于在上一卷问世后不久又有雅可比文集新一卷出版感到高兴，并祝愿这位高贵的老人以及公众在这项事业不受打扰的延续中一切顺利。——本第三卷包含四篇著述，按序言的说法，它们「在某种程度上同时产生、不过是彼此分开罢了，是一个整体的各部分，而这个整体又在每个部分中以另一种方式重复自身」。
它们是：1. 1799 年出版的雅可比致费希特的信；2.
我们在莱因霍尔德的《论文集》等处首先读到的那篇论文（31. Heft 1801）
，即《论把理性带向知性、从而给哲学以全新观点的批判主义事业》；3.
《论李希滕贝格的一则预言》，最初印于 1801 年；4.
《论神圣之物及其显现》一书，附有本次新版的前言。
另外还附有 23 封致约翰·
穆勒、G[eorg]·福斯特、赫尔德、康德的信（其中也有一封是康德致雅可比的），枢密
顾问施洛瑟、J[ohann] G[eorg]·雅可比以及若干未具名者的信，这些信为该卷作结。

en: One might perhaps have wished that in the sequence of this collection the earlier writing of Jacobi, the Letters on the Doctrine of Spinoza119), had been placed before the essays contained in the present volume, since these letters attach themselves to an interest of the age which in point of appearance is older than the philosophical figures with which those essays occupy themselves, namely to the Leibnizian-Wolffian metaphysics which had sunk to the last degree of lassitude, and in which Jacobi's philosophy at the same time has the common starting point which it shares with the Kantian philosophy, which it later confronted.

The letters mentioned also set forth, in a certain exposition and grounding, Jacobi's view of the nullity of all scientific knowledge of the divine - a view which holds sway in the writings before us not merely restricted to the philosophical systems dealt with in them, but in its entire generality, and which, accompanied by so much spirit and warmth, [also] occurs there; yet it leaves room for further wishes on the part of those who are accustomed still to ask for reasons for the truth; the placing of the letters first could have been regarded as more of an honour than the placing first of the dialogue of David Hume on faith in the second volume, which this habit of his still calls forth.

The manner in which it is to be shown in the present review how Jacobi confronts the philosophies treated of in the volume before us will gain in clarity and vividness if we have first called to mind how his mind plunged into the study of Spinozism and in this occupation fixed the standpoint at which the Kantian philosophy, already finished in itself, met him on its appearance.
To elucidate this, however, something about the state of philosophy at that time has to be recalled to memory.
zh: 人们或许本来会希望，在这套丛书的次第之中，雅可比较早的著作《致门德尔松论斯宾诺莎学说的书信》119)被置于本卷所收诸篇之前；因为这些书信所系的乃是一种时代的关切，按其出现的先后来看，它比那些论文所讨论的哲学形态更为古老，也就是那种已沉落到极度衰竭的莱布尼茨—沃尔夫式形而上学；雅可比的哲学与康德哲学正是在这里有着它们共同的出发点，而它后来曾与康德哲学相对峙。

上述书信还以某种阐释与论证的方式呈现了雅可比关于一切对神者的科学认识皆属无意义的看法——这一看法在眼前这些著述中并非仅仅局限于其中所处理的那些哲学体系，而是以其全部的普遍性居于支配地位，并且它[也]以如此丰富的精神与热忱伴随而出现；但对于那些习惯于对真理仍然追问根据的人来说，它容许还有进一步的愿望；把这些书信前置，能被看作他这一积习至今仍在赢得的一项敬意，而且比把大卫·休谟论信仰的对话前置到第二卷更胜一筹。
在当前这篇评述中应当展示雅可比如何与本卷所处理的那些哲学相对峙；这一方式若我们先行忆及其精神如何深入对斯宾诺莎主义的研究，并在这一研究中固定了他自己的立足点——康德哲学在其出现之际正是在这一点上与他相遇，尽管它自身已然完备——便会获得更多的清晰与生动。
为阐明这一点，尚须把当时哲学的状况回想起来一些。

en: French philosophy had abandoned the great spirit of the Cartesian cogito ergo sum, of knowing thought as the ground of being and of recognizing the configurations of the latter only from and in that, and had taken the reverse path of Lockeanism, deriving thought from what is immediately given in the world of appearance.

Insofar as the need still remained to grasp even here one general ground, there was pronounced as the fundamental being a conceptless universality, namely an indeterminate nature, or rather a nature to which the whole superficiality of a few paltry determinations of reflection about wholes, forces, composition and the like forms of externality and mechanism was fastened.

German culture had, in the matter itself, taken the same direction, and the Enlightenment dissolved the traditions of venerable teaching and custom, the received and immediately given content of a divine world, on all sides, and abandoned and rejected this so-called positive, because and insofar as self-consciousness was not in it or, which is the same, because self-consciousness did not find itself in it.

What remained was the death's-head of an abstract empty being which cannot be recognized, i.e. in which thinking does not have itself; the being-in-and-for-itself was thereby in fact reduced to nothing, for what self-consciousness found in itself were finite purposes and utility as the relation of all things to such purposes.

Others were content with this contagion, opposing to it their religious feeling, also attributing the theoretical results to errors which the act of recognizing commits, and seeking perhaps to support and save the truth through the correction and improvement of its recognition.

Jacobi, by contrast, opposed not only the firmness of his disposition, but the deep thoroughness of his mind did not stay with the barren remains in which metaphysics eked out a tired life and still nourished stale hopes; it rather grasped philosophy at its sources of knowledge and plunged into its most vigorous solidity.

However much the philosophical effort may otherwise struggle in the materials of metaphysics with analysing, distinguishing or joining together, with inventing possibilities of thought and refuting other possibilities, - if it does not have as its ground that solid infinite intuition and knowledge of the one substantial which Spinozism is and in whose possession we see Jacobi, and does not measure all further determinations by it, then that relation is lacking through which alone all determinations of knowledge receive truth, the relation which Spinoza so emphatically expresses: that everything must be considered under the shape of the eternal.

Jacobi appeared with this marked superiority in the time of the former metaphysics, because that solidity of intuition was native to him, whereas others placed the interest of recognition in a few paltry, conceptless determinations of understanding about being, possibility, concept and the like.
It makes no difference that God was in this the object and the goal; since he is to be comprehended through determinations of this kind, they are what constitutes the content of the knowledge.
The idea of God itself remains, apart from such finite content, a mere representation or feeling which, according to its infinity, does not enter into that knowledge.

In the one Absolute, however, these finities of content and thereby equally of the subjective striving are consumed with them; the spirit reaches that Absolute only and becomes consciousness of reason by recognizing these its limitations as null, as forms of mere appearance and thus sinking them into that abyss. - Jacobi had reached this highest intuition not merely in feeling and in representation - a form in which mere religiosity comes to a stop - but had recognized with Spinoza, through the higher path of thought, that it is the last true result of thinking, that every consistent philosophizing must lead to Spinozism.
zh: 法国哲学已经放弃了笛卡尔「cogito ergo sum」的那种宏大精神——即把思维认作存在的根据、并且只从这一根据中并只在这一根据中认识存在的诸种形态——转而走上了洛克主义相反的道路，即从现象世界中直接给予的东西推导出思维。
只要人们还感到需要在此也把握住一个普遍的根据，就有一个无概念的普遍性被宣说为那个根本性的存在者，即一种不确定的自然——或者不如说，一种自然，几项关于整体、力量、组合以及诸如此类外在性与机械性形式的贫乏反思规定之全部肤浅性都被系在它上面。
德国的教养在事情本身的方向上采取了同样的路向；而启蒙运动把那些可敬的学说与习俗的传统、把一个神圣世界所领受并直接给予的内容从四面八方化解掉了，并且放弃与抛弃了这个所谓的实证，因为并且就其而言自我意识并不在其中——或者说这乃是一回事，因为自我意识在自身中并未寻得它。
所剩下的，乃是一个抽象的空无本质的骷髅，一个无法被认识的本质，即思维在其中并无自身的本质；那个自在自为的存在者由此实际上被归结为无，因为自我意识在自身中所寻得的，乃是有限的目的以及有用性——即一切事物与此类目的之间所构成的关系。
另一些人则满足于这种传染，他们以自己的宗教感觉与之相对抗，也把理论上的结果归咎于认识行为所犯的错误，并且试图通过纠正与改进对真理的认识来支撑和拯救真理。
雅可比则相反，他不仅以自己心境的坚定与之相对抗，而且他精神的深刻与扎实也没有停留于形而上学在那空壳的残余中所勉强维持的疲惫生活、也仍在那里喂养着陈腐希望的东西；毋宁说，他在知识的源头把握住哲学，并沉潜到它那最有力量的扎实本质之中。
无论哲学的努力在形而上学的材料中如何忙于分析、区分或缝合，忙于发明思想的可能性并驳斥另一些可能性——如果它并不以那作为斯宾诺莎主义之所是、我们在雅可比身上看到其据有的那个唯一实体之扎实的无限直观与认识为根据，也不以它来衡量所有进一步的规定——那么就缺少了那种唯有借着它一切认识的规定才得以获得真理的关系，即斯宾诺莎如此直白地表达出来的关系：一切都必须在永恒的形态之下加以观照。
雅可比在旧形而上学的时代以这种杰出的优越性登场，因为那种直观的扎实性是他所固有的，而别人却把认识的关切安放在若干关于定在、可能性、概念以及诸如此类的贫乏无概念的知性规定上。
上帝在这里是对象与目的这一点并不造成差别；既然上帝应当通过这类规定来把握，那么这些规定就是构成认识内容的东西。
上帝的观念本身在这种有限内容之外仍只是一项单纯的表象或感觉，它依其无限性并不进入那种认识。

然而在唯一的绝对者中，这些内容上的有限性、因而也同样是主观劳作上的有限性，都与它们一同被消除了；精神只有当它把这些限制认识为无意义的、认识为纯粹现象的形式，从而把它们沉入那个深渊时，才达到那个绝对者并成为理性的意识。——雅可比并非只在感觉与表象中达到这一最高的直观——单纯的宗教性就停留于这种形式——，而是与斯宾诺莎一起，沿着思维的更高道路认识到：它就是思维最后真实的成果，一切贯彻到底的哲学活动都必然导向斯宾诺莎主义。

en: Here, however, the great difference enters, that the one absolute substance is apprehended only as the next form of the necessary result and that one must go beyond it.

In Jacobi therefore there manifested itself the equally firm feeling that the true, in this its first immediacy, is insufficient for the spirit, which is not an immediate being, that it has not yet been comprehended as the absolute spirit.
The object, as it is taken up by sensible consciousness, is the believed being of finite things.
But consciousness advancing to reason rejects such truth of the immediate and the belief of sensibility.
Being raised to infinity is the pure abstraction of thinking, and this thinking of pure being is not sensible intuition but intellectual or rational intuition.

But since infinite being in this immediacy is only the abstract, the motionless, the spiritless, the free, as that which determines itself out of itself, misses itself in that abyss into which all determinacy has been thrown and shattered; freedom is immediately personality to itself, as the infinite point of self-determination.

In the one solid substance, however, or in the pure intuition, which is the same as abstract thinking, only the one side of freedom is contained, namely the side which has only just come from the finities of being and consciousness to the simple element of universality, but has not yet posited self-determination and personality in it.

For it helps nothing that in the absolute substance thinking, the principle of freedom and personality, is as much an attribute as being or extension; because the substance is the undivided and undifferentiable unity of them, its fundamental determination is again only immediacy or being.
From this being, therefore, no transition to understanding and to the individual is contained.
The demand lying closer to hand would be that a transition from the absolute One to the divine attributes were demonstrated.
But it is merely assumed that there are such attributes, and further that there are a finite understanding or imagination and in them individual and finite things.

Their being is indeed always taken back and submerged as an untrue in the infinity of the substance - they thereby have the position of a given starting point for this recognition of their negativity -, but conversely the absolute substance is not apprehended as a starting point for differences, individualization, individuation, at all for all differences however they may appear, as attributes and modes, as being and thinking, understanding, imagination and so on. Everything therefore merely perishes in the substance; it is motionless in itself and returns nothing from it.
zh: 但正是在这里出现了那个重大的差别：唯一的绝对实体只是作为必然结果的下一形式来把握的，因此必须越出它。
因此在雅可比身上显露出同样坚定的感觉：真理在这种最初的直接性上对于精神——精神不是一个直接者——是不足的，真理还没有被把握为绝对的精神。
对象，就其被感性意识所接受而言，是被相信的有限事物的存在。
但向理性推进的意识却摈弃了直接者的这种真理与感性的信仰。
被提升到无限的存在，是思维的纯粹抽象；而这一对纯粹存在的思维并非感性直观，而是理智直观或理性直观。
但由于无限的存在在这种直接性上不过是抽象的、不动的、无精神的，自由者——即那从自身出发规定自身者——便在那一切规定性被抛入并撞碎其中的深渊里失却了自己；自由直接就是自身的人格性，作为自我规定的无限点。
然而在唯一的那个扎实实体中、或者说在纯粹直观中（这与抽象思维是同一回事），所包含的只是自由的一个侧面，即那仅仅刚从存在与意识的有限性上升到普遍性的单纯要素的那一面，而它尚未在其中设定自我规定与人格性。
因为在绝对实体中，思维——自由与人格性的原则——作为属性与存在或广延并无二致，这并没有帮助；由于实体是二者无差别、不可分辨的统一，它的根本规定依旧是直接性，即存在。
因此，从这个存在中并不包含任何向知性与向个别者的过渡。
更为切近的要求则是：应当展示出从绝对的一者向那些神圣属性的过渡。
但这里只是假定了存在这样的属性，并且进一步假定了存在一种有限的知性或想象力，以及在它们之中有个别的、有限的事物。
它们的存在固然总是被收回，并作为不真者被沉入实体的无限之中——这样它们在这次对其否定性的认识中便具有一个既定的出发点的地位——但反过来，绝对实体并不是被理解为差异、个别化、个体化的出发点，也不是被理解为一切差异（无论它们以何种面貌出现：作为属性与样式，作为存在与思维、知性、想象力等等）的出发点。因此，一切在实体中都只是消逝；它自身是静止的，并不从自身返回任何东西。

en: It is indeed in truth a simple consideration which lets one recognize in itself the principle of sundering - a consideration of only what the substance contains, so to speak, in fact.

For insofar as it has been recognized as the truth of the individual things which are lifted up and annihilated in it, the absolute negativity, which is the source of freedom, is the determination already posited in it itself. - What matters here is only to grasp correctly the position and significance of the negative.

If it is taken merely as the determinacy of finite things (omnis determinatio est negatio), the representation is thereby driven out of the absolute substance, has allowed the finite things to fall out of it and holds them outside it.

But in this way the negation, insofar as it is the determinacy of finite things, is not apprehended as being in the infinite or in the substance, which is rather the lifted-up-being of finite things. - But how, on the contrary, the negation is in the substance, this has already been said, and the systematic advance in philosophizing consists in nothing else than in knowing what one has already said oneself; - the substance is to be the being of the lifted-up finite, and by this one says that it is the negation of the negation, since to the finite only the negation is allotted; as the negation of the negation the substance is thereby the absolute affirmation and equally immediately freedom and self-determination. - The difference whether the Absolute is determined only as substance or as spirit consists accordingly solely in the difference whether the thinking which annihilates its finities and mediations, negates its negations and thus comprehends the one Absolute, possesses the consciousness of what it has already done in the recognition of the absolute substance, or whether it does not have this consciousness. - Jacobi had made this transition from the absolute substance to the absolute spirit in his inmost being and had cried out with an irresistible feeling of certainty: God is spirit, the Absolute is free and personal. - With a view to philosophical insight it was of the greatest importance that through him the moment of the immediacy of the knowledge of God was brought out in the most definite and vigorous way.

God is not a dead but a living God; he is still more than the living one, he is spirit and the eternal love, and he is this alone through the fact that his being is not the abstract but the distinguishing which moves within itself and the recognition of himself in the person distinguished from him; and his essence is only the immediate, i.e. existing, unity, insofar as it eternally leads back that eternal mediation to unity, and this leading back is itself this unity, the unity of life, self-feeling, of personality, of knowledge of oneself.

A dead, sensible thing is only an immediacy, and not through the mediation of itself with itself. - Yet in Jacobi the transition from mediation to immediacy has rather the form of an external discarding and rejecting of the mediation.

In this respect it is the reflecting consciousness which, separated from the rational intuition, removes that mediating movement of recognition from this intuition; indeed it goes further and even declares it to be something which is obstructive and corrupting for this intuition.

Here two acts are to be distinguished: firstly finite recognition itself, which has to do only with objects and forms which are not in and for themselves but are conditioned and grounded through something other, - a recognition whose character is therefore mediation; the second recognition is then the reflection just named, which recognizes both the objects and the subjective modes of knowing of the first as a content and as forms of mediation and thereby as not absolute.

This second recognition is therefore on the one hand itself mediated, for it is essentially related to that first recognition, has it as its precondition and object; on the other hand it is the lifting up of that first recognition, - that is, as was said before, a mediating which is the lifting-up of mediation, or such a lifting-up of mediation only insofar as it is itself a mediating.

Recognition, as the lifting-up of mediation, is just thereby immediate recognition; if it does not apprehend its immediacy in this way, it is not apprehended that it is in this way alone the immediacy of reason and not of a stone.

In natural consciousness the knowledge of God may have the appearance of a merely immediate knowledge; it may equate the immediacy in which the spirit is its own to the immediacy of its perception of the stone; but the business of philosophical knowledge is to recognize what truly the doing of that consciousness consists in, - to recognize that in it that immediacy is a living, spiritual immediacy and comes forth only in a mediation which lifts itself up.
Natural consciousness lacks this insight quite as much as it, being organically living, digests without possessing the science of physiology.

It seems that Jacobi was led by the form of the proofs of God, which were formerly called the proofs of the existence of God, to the supposition that consciousness was thereby required [to believe] that it could have no knowledge of God without having formally gone through the series of inferences, presupposed concepts and conclusions which those proofs contained, - precisely, as just recalled, as if one demanded of man [the belief] that he could not digest, nor walk, nor see, nor hear, without having studied anatomy and physiology.

A misunderstanding connected with this is that the knowledge of God and the being of God himself have been made through the mediation of recognition into something dependent, grounded in something other.

This apparent disproportion, however, is already lifted up through the matter itself; for since God is the result, this mediation itself is on the contrary explained in it as lifting itself up through itself.

What is the last is recognized as the first; the end is the purpose; through the fact that it is invented as the purpose, and indeed as the absolute final purpose, this product is rather explained as that which immediately moves first.

This going forward to a result is thereby just as much the going back into itself, the counter-stroke against itself; it is that which was stated above as the only nature of the spirit, as of the acting final purpose which brings itself forth.

If he were a being without working, an immediacy, he would not be spirit, not even life; if he were not purpose and a working according to purposes, he would not find in his product that this working is only a coming-together with himself, only a mediation through which their determinacy is mediated to immediacy.
zh: 但这确实是一个简单的考察，它让人在自身之中认出了分化的原则——一个只考察实体（可以说，就事实而言）所包含之物的考察。
因为它既已被认识为那些在它之中被扬弃并被抹消的个别事物的真理，那作为自由之源的绝对否定性就是已经设定在它自身中的规定。——这里要紧的只是正确地看清否定者的地位与意义。
如果只把它当作有限事物的规定性来把握（omnis determinatio est negatio），那么表象就由此被从绝对实体中排了出去，有限事物被任其从中掉落出来，并被保持在它之外。

但这样一来，否定性——就其作为有限事物的规定性而言——就并没有被把握为处在无限者或实体之中；实体毋宁是有限事物的被扬弃。——反过来，否定性如何处在实体之中，这一点已经说过了；而在哲学中系统地推进，归根结底无非在于知道人们自己已经说过的东西；——实体应当是有限者的被扬弃，由此人们就说，它是否定的否定，因为分派给有限者的只有否定；作为否定的否定，实体于是就是绝对的肯定，同样直接地就是自由与自我规定。——绝对者究竟只是被规定为实体还是被规定为精神，这一差别归根结底只在于：那个摧毁自身的有限性与中介、否定自身的否定性并由此把握唯一的绝对者的思维，是否具有它在对绝对实体的认识中已经做过之事的意识；还是它并不具有这种意识。——雅可比在他内在最深处完成了这一从绝对实体到绝对精神的过渡，并以一种不可抗拒的确定性之感呼喊道：上帝是精神，绝对者是自由而有人格的。——就哲学洞见而言，极其重要的是，通过他，对上帝的认识之直接性这一环节被以最确定、最有力的方式凸显了出来。
上帝不是死板的上帝，而是活生生的上帝；他还不止是活着的那一位，他就是精神与永恒的爱；而他之所以是这两者，只在于他的存在并非那抽象的存在，而是在自身中运动着的区分以及在与他相区别的人格中对自己自身的认识；而他的本质只是那直接的、亦即存在着的统一，就其把那种永恒的中介永远导回统一而言；而这一导回本身就是这一统一，即生命、自我感受、人格性以及对自己的知识的统一。
一个死的、感性的物只是直接者，却并不是通过它与自身的中介而是的。——然而在雅可比那里，从中介到直接性的过渡更多地具有外在的摒弃与拒斥这种中介的形式。
就此而言，正是那种反思的意识——它与理性直观相分离——把认识中那种中介着的运动从这一直观中移走；它甚至走得更远，甚至宣称那种运动是对这一直观有所妨碍并加以败坏的东西。
这里有两个行为需要区分：第一是有限的认识本身，它只与那些并非自在自为、而是通过他者才得到限定与奠基的对象与形式打交道——因此一种以中介为特征的认识；第二个认识便是刚才所说的反思，它把第一个认识的对象以及主观的认知方式都认识为一个内容、认识为中介的形式，因而认识为非绝对的。
因此这第二个认识一方面本身也是有中介的，因为它本质上关联于那第一个认识，并以之为自己的前提与对象；另一方面它又是对那第一个认识的扬弃——即如前所述，是一种为「对中介的扬弃」而中介的调节，或者说，仅就它本身是一种中介而言，才是这样的中介之扬弃。
认识作为对中介的扬弃，正是因此才是直接的认识；如果它不是这样来把握自己的直接性，那么就没有被把握到：唯有这样，它才是理性的直接性，而不是一块石头的直接性。
在自然意识中，对上帝的知识也许显得像是某种单纯直接的知识；它也许把精神据以是它自己的那种直接性，等同于它对石头的知觉的直接性；但哲学知识的事务在于认识那种意识的活动真正何在——认识到：在它之中那种直接性乃是一种活生生的、精神性的直接性，并且只在一种自我扬弃的中介中才显现出来。
自然意识同样缺乏这种洞见，就像它作为有机生命体那样在不具备生理学这门学问的情况下进行消化。
看来，雅可比是因那些上帝认识的形式——它们早先被称为「上帝的存在之证明」——而被引向了这样一种设想：仿佛意识因此被要求[相信]，若不形式地走完那些证明所包含的推理、前设概念与结论的系列，它就不可能对上帝有任何知识；——恰如刚才所忆及的，仿佛人们要求人[相信]，若未曾研习解剖学与生理学，他就不可能消化、行走、观看、聆听。
与此相联的一个误解是：把对上帝的知识以及上帝自身的存在通过认识的中介变成了一个依赖的、在另一个者之中有根据的东西[了]。
但这一表面的不相应本身已由事情本身所扬弃；因为既然上帝就是结果，那么这种中介本身反倒在其中显现为通过自身而扬弃自身。
那最后者被认识为最初者；终点就是目的；由于它被设定为目的，甚至被设定为绝对的终极目的，这一产物反倒被解释为那最初、直接推动着的东西。
这样，向一个成果的推进同时也就是向自身的返回、对自身的反冲；这正是前面所说的精神的唯一本性，即那把自己产生出来的、起作用的终极目的所具有的本性。
如果他没有作用、只是一个直接的存在，那么他就不是精神，甚至不是生命；如果他不是目的、不是依目的而起作用，那么他就不会在其产物中发现：这种作用不过是与自身的会合，只不过是一种中介，通过这种中介，它们的规定性被中介为直接性。

en: Since Jacobi then throws away the mediation which is in recognition and does not restore it to himself within the nature of the spirit as its essential moment, his consciousness of the absolute spirit holds fast in the form of immediate, merely substantial knowledge.
The simple fundamental intuition of Spinozism has substantiality for its only content.

If, however, the intuition of the Absolute knows itself as intellectual, i.e. as recognizing intuition, and if further its object and content is not the rigid substance but the spirit, then the mere form of the substantiality of knowledge, namely its immediacy, would equally have to be thrown away.

For precisely by the life and the knowing movement within itself does the absolute spirit alone distinguish itself from the absolute substance, and the knowledge of it is only something spiritual, intellectual. - It is now chiefly by the determination of spirit which Jacobi finds in his rational intuition that he measures the philosophical systems which he makes the object of the essays contained in the present volume.
He expresses towards these philosophies not only the content but just as pertinaciously this substantial form of his rational intuition.
It is the Kantian, the Fichtean and the philosophy of nature which are here considered by him, and the fundamental character of his mode of treatment is designated by what has been stated.
zh: 由于雅可比把认识中那种中介丢开，并不把它在精神的本性之内作为精神的本质环节重新恢复给自己，他对绝对精神的意识便固着在直接的、纯粹实体性的知识形式上。
斯宾诺莎主义那单纯的基本直观，以实体性为其唯一的内容。
然而，如果对绝对者的直观自知是理智的、亦即认识的直观，并且它的对象与内容并非僵硬的实体而是精神，那么知识的实体性这一单纯形式，即知识的直接性，也同样必须被丢掉。
因为恰恰是凭借自身内在的生命与求知的运动，绝对精神才与绝对实体区别开来，而对它的知识只是一种精神性的、理智性的东西。——雅可比主要以他在理性直观中所发现的精神的规定为准绳，来衡量那些他以本卷所收诸篇为对象的哲学体系。
他面对这些哲学体系所表述的，不只是它们的内容，同样也固执地表述着他那理性直观的实体形式。
他在这里所考察的乃是康德哲学、费希特哲学与自然哲学，而他的处理方式的根本特征已由上述各项所标明。

en: The essays themselves are only too well known to the public; but the passion of the age in which they appeared may be considered as having passed by; the consideration of their moments may therefore be all the shorter and also less compromising, and may confine itself to the essential.

The present collection and the study of it must not seem superfluous because a part of the philosophies to which it refers has passed away; I also see with regret Jacobi speaking on S. 340 in a tone to the effect that it is well known how rapidly the philosophical systems have changed in Germany during the last 25 years.

For this is customarily above all the language of those who justify their contempt for philosophy not only to themselves but wish to take credit to themselves for the fact that indeed the philosophical systems contradict each other so greatly and change so often, that it is therefore a simple piece of prudence not to have anything to do with them, the more so since this having anything to do with them means to want to seek and have something perishable in something so perishable, rather than something imperishable, truth. - What indeed is perishable and has been perishable are the many-coloured strivings to philosophize without philosophy and to have a philosophy.

Yet this perishable itself can also be looked upon as imperishable, the change as perennial. - Jacobi's assertions of the incapacity of science to recognize the divine cannot indeed be absolved of this consequence, that ignorance and spiritlessness have accepted such sentences as a convenient cushion and have made of them a good conscience and even pride, just as the Kantian philosophy has reduced the object to a problematic Something and has secured for it, as thing-in-itself, an otium cum dignitate to enjoy, in a witty phrase of Jacobi's (S. 74).
zh: 这些论文本身对公众来说已经再熟悉不过了；但它们出现时那个时代的热忱可以看作已经过去；因此对其各个环节的考察可以更为简短，也可以少些顾虑，而只限于本质之处。
不能因为本卷所涉及的那些哲学中有一部分已经过时，就认为这一集子及其研究是多余的；我也不乐见雅可比在 S. 340 处以那种口吻说，人们都知道这 25 年来德国的哲学体系更换得何等之快。
因为这通常尤其是那些人的说法：他们不仅在自己面前为其对哲学的轻蔑辩护，还想就这一点为自己邀功——哲学体系之间如此相互抵触、又如此频繁地更换，因此不与之交手乃是一种简单的明智；更何况这种交手的意思是要在如此易逝之物中寻求并要有一个易逝之物，而不是不逝的真理。——真正易逝、并且一向易逝的，正是那些五花八门的努力：没有哲学而要哲学化，并且要有一套哲学。
然而这一易逝者本身也可以被看作不逝的，这一更替也可以被看作恒常的。——雅可比关于科学无力认识神者的那些断言，大概不能免于这样一项后果：无知与无心智把这样的句子当作一块舒适的软垫接受下来，并从中造出一种良好的良心乃至高傲；正如康德哲学把对象降低为一个成问题的某物，并且按照雅可比的一句妙语（S. 74），为它作为自在之物挣得一份 otium cum dignitate（尊严的闲适）可供享受。

en: The Kantian philosophy is chiefly the object of the second essay, whose title has been given above; the other essays, particularly the third, however, also repeatedly return to it.

I want to speak of it first, as of the first, and of Jacobi's polemic against it, and to indicate briefly why its theses, measured by Jacobi's great standpoint that the Absolute is to be comprehended as spirit, must appear to him very inadequate.
For what this philosophy finds as the highest on the theoretical path, i.e. in a recognition of what is, are in general mere appearances.

But its essential features prove to be three determinations into which it is analyzed, namely firstly a thing-in-itself to which no further determination whatever accrues than that of being this quite conceptless thing-in-itself, secondly the I of self-consciousness insofar as it makes connections out of itself, but in doing so is conditioned by a given manifold and produces only finite connections of the finite, finally the other extreme to the pure thing-in-itself, the I as pure unity.
Kant called the I in that finite activity understanding, the I as pure unity reason.

The two extremes of the syllogism, in which the recognition of what is is represented, the thing-in-itself and the pure unity of self-consciousness, are thus abstract universalities; and so fixed they are absolutely something spiritless.

Likewise the middle of the syllogism is indeed something concrete, but for that very reason an external coming-together and bringing-together of ingredients which remain essentially external to one another; just as little therefore is here to be recognized a spirit certain of itself, or certain of the other as of a truth.

For the knowledge of what ought to be, of the practical, Kant found in self-consciousness that same formal unity which constituted the one extreme of the preceding syllogism, as the principle by which the good and the duty are to be constituted.
Over against this principle a manifold nature makes up the other extreme; the concrete general unity of these extremes remains in the Kantian system a beyond.

The inner certainty of itself alone and the reality found as external are preserved as simply separated and truly being; and the unity of what is and of what ought to be, of existence and of concept, can for that reason come forth only as a perennial postulate, not as what is true.
The practical therefore has not the spirit as its last result either, and thus, as was explained above, the spirit does not find itself in it as the first ground and truth.
zh: 康德哲学主要是第二篇论文的对象，其标题已在上文给出；但其他诸篇、尤其是第三篇，也同样屡次回到它。
我想先谈它——作为首要的对象——以及雅可比针对它的论争，并简要说明：为什么它的那些命题，以雅可比那个伟大立场——即应把绝对者把握为精神——来衡量，对他来说必定显得极为不足。
因为这门哲学在理论的道路上、即在对「所是者」的认识中所发现的最高者，一般说来不过是现象。
然而其本质却显出三项规定，它被分析为这三项：其一是一个自在之物，除了「是这全然无概念的自在之物」之外再没有任何别的规定归于它；其二是自我意识的我，就其从自身作出联结而言，但在此它受制于一个既定的杂多，因而只产生有限者的有限联结；其三则是与纯粹自在之物相对的另一极端，即作为纯粹统一的我。
康德把处在那种有限活动中的我称作知性，把作为纯粹统一的我称作理性。
推论的两个极端——对「所是者」的认识正是由此得到表述——即自在之物与自我意识的纯粹统一，因而都是抽象的普遍性；而如此被固定下来，它们就全然是无精神的东西。
同样，推论的中项固然是一个具体之物，但恰恰因此它只是些本质上都彼此外在的成分在外在上的会合与凑合；因此在这里也同样无从认出一个对自身有把握、或把他者作为真理而有把握的精神。
而对于「所应者」的知识、即实践的知识，康德在自我意识中所找到的，正是构成前一个推论之一极端的那种形式统一，把它当作那种借以构成善与义务的原则。
与这一原则相对，一个多方面的自然构成了另一个极端；这两个极端的具体统一在康德体系中仍然是一个彼岸。
仅仅对自身的内在确定性，与那作为外在而被发现的现实性，被保持为绝对分开的、并且真实存在着的两者；因此，「所是者」与「所应者」、即定在与概念的统一，只能作为一个恒常的设定要求而出现，而不能作为那真实者而出现。
因此实践也并没有把精神作为它最后的结果；这样一来，正如前文所解释的，精神并不在其中把自己认作最初的基础与真理。

en: Jacobi, then, did not merely apply his standard to the Kantian philosophy as something presupposed, but treated it too in the true way, namely dialectically.
The Kantian determination of the form in which the task of philosophy was to be conceived and solved provided the weapon for this immediately.
Kant raised the question: how are synthetic judgements a priori possible?, instead of determining the necessity of such judgements as the object of philosophy.

He shared the formulation of the task with the method of the metaphysics of his time, which believed it had first of all to demonstrate the possibility of the concepts, and so also of the concept of God.
Underneath such a possibility, since it is still to be kept separate from actuality and necessity and is thereby an abstractum, lies the abstract identity, the formal unity of understanding.

Jacobi takes up this form and holds fast, in the dry understanding in which they occur, space as one, time as one, consciousness as one whose pure synthesis, the synthesis in itself, independent of thesis and antithesis, i.e. the quite abstract copula is, is, is, without beginning and end, and asks now with good reason how here the possibility that a knot be tied could obtain.

Indeed, if the white is to be only white and the black opposite only black, it is not possible that a grey or any other colour arise or exist. - Moreover Jacobi now describes such abstractions with equal right as empty thought-things, as shadows and witch-mist. - Only he stops at considering the nullity of abstract space, abstract time, abstract identity and abstract difference as his own reflection, external to these abstractions.
This is all the more consistent in that the dialectic here was directed only against the Kantian presentation and only its equally abstract nothing was to come out of it.
But the nullity immanent in such abstractions would have been the objective dialectic of them and would have led to the necessity of the concrete, of that which is here called the synthetic a priori.

The proof of the impossibility of the concrete, which is drawn from the presupposed validity of those thought-things, would accordingly have been turned by means of their demonstrated untruth into the opposite, into the proof of the necessity of the concrete. - Moreover the concrete then also occurs in relation to those abstractions as imagination, judging, apperception of self-consciousness.

For this relation, since the abstractions are fixed as existing in and for themselves, it now results that they, and equally the concrete things, held abstractly fast in their difference, are a non-self-lifting-up, non-dialectical but existing ground for one another, - that reason rests on understanding, understanding on imagination, imagination on sensibility, and sensibility again on imagination. - It could however still be disputed whether the relation of condition and conditioned does not express more exactly the relation in which those powers appear as opposed to one another in Kant. - More important, however, it is not to overlook in this treatment of the Kantian critique of reason that its infinite merit has been marked out, namely that it has recognized the freedom of the spirit as a principle also on the theoretical side.
This principle, admittedly in an abstract form, lies in the idea of an originally-synthetic apperception of self-consciousness, which also in recognition essentially wants to be self-determining.

However abstract this theoretical freedom is, it is no more abstract than the moral one, of which Jacobi says on S. 324 that it is indeed the faculty in man 'by which he has his life within himself, is conscious of a power to overcome every resistance to the good, - but it is partly conditioned by a resistance, partly does not come to actuality and is only an approximation and a striving'. - This side is mentioned incidentally in so far as on S. 80 it is said that an original synthesizing would be an original determining; this concept, however, is there thereby eliminated by the statement that an original determining would be a creation out of nothing.

With this consequence, or rather with the expression creation out of nothing, however, the concept of freedom in the theoretical can be all the less dismissed, since the moral freedom would be dismissed with it.
zh: 雅可比对康德哲学并非只是把他自己的尺度当作预设之物套用上去，而是也以真正的方式、亦即以辩证的方式对待它。
康德对「哲学的任务应当如何被把握与解决」这一形式的规定，本身就直接提供了对它的武器。
康德提出了这样的问题：先天综合判断（a priori）是如何可能的？他并没有把这类判断的必然性规定为哲学的对象。
他把任务的这种设定与当时形而上学的方法共享，后者认为首先必须证明诸概念——因而也包括上帝这一概念——的可能性。
这样一种可能性——因为它仍须与现实性和必然性分开，因而是一个抽象物——其底下潜着的是那种抽象的同一性，即知性的形式统一。
雅可比承接了这种形式，并按照它们在其中出现的那种干瘪的知性，把空间固定为「一者」，把时间固定为「一者」，把意识固定为「一者」——其纯粹的综合、就其自身而言独立于正题与反题的综合，也就是那全然抽象的系词「是、是、是」，没有开端也没有终结；于是他理所当然地质问：在这里，打一个结的可能性究竟怎么可能成立？
的确，如果白只是白、黑相对只是黑，那么灰色或别的任何颜色就不可能产生，也不可能存在。——此外，雅可比同样有理由地把这类抽象描述为空洞的思想之物、描述为影子与妖雾。——只是他到此为止，把抽象空间、抽象时间、抽象同一性与抽象差异的无意义看作他本人的、位于这些抽象之外的反思。
这一点恰恰是极为一贯的，因为这里的辩证法只针对康德的表述而发，所得出的也只应是同样抽象的虚无。
然而内在于这类抽象之中的无意义，本来就会是它们自身的客观辩证法，并且会导向具体者的必然性，即这里所称的「a priori 的综合者」。
那个从这些思想之物的先验有效性出发而得出的、关于具体者之不可能性的证明，就会借助它们所显示的不真而转到它的反面，即转为关于具体者之必然性的证明。——此外，具体者于是也以想象力、判断、对自我意识的统觉这些形式，相对于那些抽象而出现。

就这一关系而言，由于抽象者被固定为自在自为地存在着，于是得出：它们以及同样地那些具体者，在其差异中又被抽象地固定住，便彼此成为那种不自我扬弃的、非辩证的、而是现成的根据——理性依存于知性，知性依存于想象力，想象力依存于感性，而感性又依存于想象力。——不过还可以争辩：条件与被条件者的关系是否更准确地表达了那些力量在康德那里彼此相对时的关系。——但更紧要的是，在对康德的理性批判作这种处理时，不应忽略它的无限功绩，即它已经把精神之自由在理论一方面也认识为一项原则。
这一原则——诚然是以抽象的形式——潜藏在一个自我意识的「原初—综合」统觉的观念里，而这一统觉在认识中同样在本质上是想要自我规定的。

这一理论上的自由无论多么抽象，它也不比道德上的自由更抽象；关于后者，雅可比在 S. 324 处说，它固然是人「凭借之而把生命持于自身之内、意识到一种克服一切对善之阻力的力量」的能力，——但它部分地受制于某种阻力，部分地又不能成为现实，因而只是一种接近与努力。——这一面在这里只是顺带提及，因为 S. 80 处说，一个原初的综合将会是一个原初的规定；不过这个概念在那里又因「一个原初的规定将是一个从无中创造」这一说法而被消除了。
然而，凭着这一推论——或者不如说，凭着「从无中创造」这一表述——人们就更不能把理论方面的自由概念打发了事，因为道德的自由也将随之被打发。

en: Yet the narrative manner of Kant, who on his standpoint at first was concerned only in general with a basis of something universal and necessary in recognition, does indeed furnish a well-grounded occasion to take the materials of his history of recognition - feeling, time and space, imagination, understanding and finally reason - as quite accidental in relation to one another, as their coming together appears in a mere history, and, by fixing them as abstract grounds, to make the contradiction effective, to bring them together and set them into one.

This spiritlessness of their apprehension, this want of the presentation to have thought of the demonstration of the necessity of these activities of spirit both in their determinacy and of the concrete of them, is what is made clear through the Jacobi criticism.

This criticism thereby acquires so much the greater significance, since even friends of Jacobi have been able to think that they have found in it even an improvement of the critical philosophy, in that the knowledge of the recognizing spirit may be made the affair of an anthropology, - of a simple narration of facts which are supposed to be found in consciousness, and recognition then consists in nothing further than in a dissection of what is found.

They thus deliberately, as if this were the right thing, give up recognizing the activities of the spirit in their necessity; whereas it is rather the lack of this necessity, the accidentality and externality in which the determinations of the spirit appear as opposed to one another in Kant, which gives Jacobi the ground of his dialectic against that synthesis as such and against the bad, finite relations which come to light at that presupposed externality of the activities of the spirit.
zh: 不过，康德那种叙述性的方式——他起初在自己的立场上关心的毕竟只是：认识中一般说来有一个普遍与必然者的根据——确实提供了一个有根据的机会：把他那认识史的材料——感觉、时间与空间、想象力、知性以及最后是理性——看作彼此完全偶然的、仿佛它们在一段单纯的历史中相遇那样，并借着把它们固定为抽象的根据而使矛盾得以成立，把它们会合起来合为一体。
正是这种对其把握的无精神、这种陈述未曾想到去展示这些精神活动之规定性的必然性以及它们之具体者的必然性，将由雅可比的批评所阐明。
这一批评因而具有更大的意义，因为甚至雅可比的朋友们也曾以为：他们从中找到了对批判哲学的一项改进——即认识着的精神的认识可以成为一门人类学的事情——成为对那些应当在意识中预先被找到的事实的单纯叙述，而认识随后便不再有别的内容，只是对所找到者加以肢解。
他们于是有意地——仿佛这才是正当的——放弃了在必然性上去认识精神的诸种活动；然而恰恰是这一必然性的欠缺、那种偶然性与外在性（精神的规定在康德那里正是这样彼此相对而出现），给了雅可比以他反对那种综合本身、以及反对在精神诸活动的这种预设的外在性中显露出来的那些糟糕的有限关系的辩证法的根据。

en: It remains accordingly to be mentioned briefly how the want of what the Kantian philosophy teaches about the practical reason is apprehended in the Jacobi essay.

For theoretical reason the ideas of God, freedom and immortality are unprovable, their objects cannot be recognized; it goes upon what is; for the knowledge of it it requires understanding, which on its side for the application of its categories requires an experience or rather a perception of the temporal and spatial and a material of feeling.
Such knowledge thus only brings it to appearances; but God, freedom and immortality do not fall into such experience and into the world of appearance.

Practical reason now postulates these ideas which are unprovable theoretically; but their subjectivity need not be postulated, for they have it as ideas; their objectivity, however, is precisely this side which belongs to recognizing reason.

The reproach of this one-sidedness of the practical is highly significant, the more so since it has almost become a prejudice that in the practical, in the impulse of the heart, alone the true is to be found, and that knowledge, science, theoretical reason are superfluous for it, indeed even harmful and dangerous.

The consciousness that God is, that freedom is, that immortality is, is something quite other than the postulate that these ideas merely ought to be; that theoretical side constitutes the complement to the ought, and only the conviction that the rational is as it is as it ought to be can constitute the ground for the practical; the bare ought, the subjective concept without objectivity, is as spiritless as a mere being without the concept, without having its being-ought in itself and being according to it, is an empty show.
zh: 因此还须简要说明：康德哲学关于实践理性所教导的东西的欠缺，在雅可比那篇论文中是如何被把握的。
对理论理性来说，上帝、自由与不朽的观念是无法证明的，它们的对象不能被认识；理论理性所涉及的乃是所是者；要认识它，就还需要知性，而知性本身为了运用其范畴，又需要一种经验——或者不如说，需要对时间性与空间性的知觉——以及一种感觉材料。
这样的认识因此只把事情带到现象；而上帝、自由与不朽并不落入这样的经验和现象世界之中。
实践理性于是设定那些在理论上无法证明的观念；但它们的主观性并不需要被设定，因为作为观念它们本就具有主观性；而它们的客观性恰恰就是那属于认识着的理性的方面。
对实践的这一偏侧性的指责极为重要，尤其是因为几乎已经成了一种偏见：以为在实践之中、在心灵的冲动里，唯独才找得到真理，而认识、知识、理论理性对它是多余的，甚至有害而危险。
意识到上帝是、自由是、不朽是，与设定这些观念「仅仅应当如此」完全是两回事；那个理论的一面构成了对「应当」的补充，而唯有「合理者所是者即是其应当所是者」这一确信，才能构成实践的基础；单纯的「应当」、没有客观性的主观概念，与一个单纯的存在——没有概念、不把其「是—应当」持于自身之内并与之相符、是空洞的假象——同样是无精神的。

en: We now turn to the letter to Fichte.

The inadequacy which is pointed out in the Fichtean philosophy in this essay, the first of the present volume, goes in the essentials back to the same thing which Jacobi contested in the Kantian philosophy.
The Fichtean system is, as is well known, raised by the Kantian into a higher abstraction and carried out more consistently.
It is an attempt to present the categories, the determinations of thought of the theoretical as well as of the practical sphere, in a systematic manner in the context of necessity.

If with Kant the object first shrinks, so to speak, through the whole course of the critique into an unknown and unknowable thing-in-itself, and is only set outside the range of understanding and then also of reason through the knowledge of these so-called faculties of the soul, then with Fichte the pure unity of the I with itself and over against it at once immediately the thing-in-itself as non-I appears equally abstractly; the further development of the forms which the determination of the one through the other assumes has that opposition persistently at its foundation, since every further form is indeed a richer synthesis of the same, but does not come to overcoming it.

These resolutions therefore remain relations and finite forms, whose last resolution likewise points across to the practical, which however is no further brought than to a one-sided willing and striving weighted down with a beyond.

Of such infinite importance in respect of its content is the Fichtean principle as a moment, or in respect of its form, that Fichte has given the Kantian principle this high abstraction; so it must, because it is to remain in its one-sidedness an absolute principle and not be reduced to a moment, also appear to the concrete spirit as something spiritless.
zh: 我们现在转向那封致费希特的信。
在本卷的第一篇论文中所指出的、费希特哲学上的不足，其本质归结为雅可比在康德哲学时所反对的那同一件事。
众所周知，费希特体系是经由康德哲学而被提升到一个更高的抽象、并且被更彻底地贯彻了的。
这是一次尝试，要在必然性的关联中系统地表述那些范畴，即理论范围与实践范围的思维规定。

如果说在康德那里，对象是在批判的整个进程中被压缩成一个未知且不可知的自在之物，并且只是通过对这些所谓灵魂能力的认识才被设定在知性、继而也在理性的范围之外，那么在费希特那里，与自身统一的纯粹的我则立即直接地出现，而与它相对、同样抽象地则出现作为非我的自在之物；形式更进一步的发展——即一个者通过另一个者而得到规定的那种发展——始终以那一对立为其根据，因为每一个更进一步的形式固然是同一者更丰富的综合，却始终达不到克服它。
因此这些化解仍然是关系与有限的形式，而它们最后的化解同样指向实践；不过实践所能达到的，也不过是一种偏侧的、带着一个彼岸的「应当」与努力而已。
费希特原则作为环节，就其内容或就其形式而言具有如此无限的重要性，以至于费希特给了康德原则这样高的抽象；因此，就它应当在自身的偏侧性中仍是绝对原则而不被降低为一个环节而言，它面对具体的精神也必定显得是同样无精神的东西。

en: Jacobi did not treat this philosophy dialectically as he treated the Kantian, although by virtue of its scientific form it would have offered itself more simply to such treatment.

For since Fichte begins with Ich = Ich as the first absolute principle of his philosophy, he lets the second follow immediately, that the I simply sets a non-I against itself, which principle in its form, namely as that of setting against, is likewise unconditional.
These two unconditioneds are just as such abstractions identical with themselves as are abstract space and abstract time or the abstract is in Kant.

Against the third principle in Fichte, which contains the synthesis of those abstractions and the ground of all following syntheses, the same impossibility could be made valid as against the Kantian synthesis.

Jacobi is content here to express his solid intuition of the absolutely concrete, of the spiritual, against that abstraction of the I which remains the same even in its synthesis, and from out of that standpoint to reject the one-sidedness of the Fichtean subjectivity.

What Jacobi on S. 40 calls the moral principle of reason, but which is properly only the principle of a reason brought down to understanding, namely the abstract concord of man with himself, he determines correctly as dreary, desolate and empty, and sets against it the faculty of ideas as not empty, the concrete reason, under the popular name heart. - In the essentials this is the same which Aristotle already blamed in the moral principle (Ήϑιϰ. μεγ. Α [Große Ethik, A]); for he says that the first teacher of morality, Socrates, made the virtues into a knowledge (ἐπιστήμη) - the good and beautiful is the practical idea only as the universal -, but this is impossible, he adds, for all knowledge is with a ground (λόγος); the ground, however, belongs to the thinking side of the spirit; it therefore happens to him that he cancels the alogical side of the soul, the impulse and the habit (πάϑος ϰαὶ ἠ ͂ϑος). - The universal of the practical contains only what ought to be; Aristotle, like Jacobi, misses in it the side of that through and according to which the universal is.

But the impulse and the habit of Aristotle say something much more determinate than the mere heart. - It has always been held to be the work of the wisest men not only to know the universal, the abstract laws, but also to have insight into what belongs to the impulse, custom and habit as their unconscious side, and to find and bring about the regulation of this side.

Through such a regulation that abstract side has a natural reality in a particular people, and the law has as custom for the individual an existing validity; so it is given both as his impulse and also for the as yet undetermined, directionless impulse.

For the more highly formed disposition and for its morality, however, a still more general knowledge is required, namely to have before oneself not only the being of a people, but to know it also as the being which appears as nature, world and history.

This is the same which was shown above as the one-sidedness of the practical principle as it is comprehended in the Kantian system, namely that it abstracts from the theoretical moment and is therefore subjective. - It may seem that Aristotle's reproach rather concerns the opposite and is directed to the point that the virtue of Socrates was made into a knowledge, i.e. that the moral principle was something theoretical. - In the first place, however, Aristotle does not reproach that what is universal in the ethical, i.e. the good, is comprehended; rather in the further pursuit he finds the consideration of it necessary, only he distinguishes this from the investigation of the virtue.

Jacobi departs from this in so far as he rejects this form of the good and a doctrine of duties and refers for it to the heart. - The good is now the immanent purpose of self-consciousness, and its being is a being-in-and-for-itself; in so far it belongs to the theoretical; but it is one-sided in so far as it is held fast in the form of universality against the concrete idea.
Its content, on the contrary, is what it ought to be, thus posited as a subjective purpose.
From this the other side is reality, the properly theoretical moment, which is found as the irrational, as nature, both as external and bodily and as inner feeling, impulse, custom, habit.

The knowledge of this nature in turn receives this form of irrationality, in so far as it lacks the concept of how it should be, does not know in it the absolute final purpose, does not know it as a mere realization and presentation of the same, - just as the good remains spiritless and does not rise above the standpoint of existence, namely of mere striving, in so far as it does not supplement itself through the view of reality.
zh: 雅可比并没有像对待康德哲学那样以辩证的方式对待这一哲学，尽管就其科学形式而言，它本来会更容易地呈现在这种处理面前。
因为费希特以「Ich = Ich」作为其哲学的第一条绝对原则开始，他随即让第二条原则跟上来，即我干脆把一个非我设定在自己对面；而这条原则就其形式而言、也就是就其「设定于对面」而言，同样是无条件的。
这两个无条件者与自身同一的抽象，正是如同康德那里的抽象空间、抽象时间或那个抽象的「是」一样。
对于费希特的第三条原则——它包含着那些抽象的综合以及一切后续综合的根据——人们同样可以像针对康德的综合那样提出同样的不可能性。
雅可比在这里只满足于：把绝对具体者、绝对精神者的那种扎实直观，针对那个即便在其综合中仍旧是同一个的我的抽象表述出来，并从那个立场出发驳斥费希特主观性的偏侧。

雅可比在 S. 40 处称作理性的道德原则的东西，实际上不过是那种被降低到知性的理性的原则，即人自身的抽象契合，他正确地把它规定为荒凉、空旷而空洞，并以观念的能力、即具体的理性与之相对——后者以通俗的名字叫作心。——归根结底，这与亚里士多德在道德原则上早已责备过的东西是同一个（Ήϑιϰ. μεγ. Α [大伦理, A]）；他说，道德的第一位教师苏格拉底把诸德性变成了知识（ἐπιστήμη）——善与美只有作为普遍者才是实践的观念——，但这是不可能的，他补充说，因为一切知识都带着一个根据（λόγος）；而根据是属于精神的思维一面的；因此对他来说就发生了这样一件事：他扬弃了灵魂的非逻辑一面，即冲动与习性（πάϑος ϰαὶ ἠ ͂ϑος）。——实践的普遍者只包含它所应当者；亚里士多德和雅可比一样，在其中缺少了那个「普遍者由之并依之而是」的方面。
但亚里士多德的冲动与习性所说的东西，比那单纯的心要具体得多。——历来人们都认为，最智慧者们的工作不仅是认识普遍者、那些抽象的法则，而且还要对那属于冲动、习俗与习性这一无意识侧面的东西有洞见，并找到和实现对这一侧面的调节。
通过这样一种调节，那抽象的一面在某个特定民族中便有了自然的实在性；而法律作为习俗对于个别者具有一种现存的有效性；这样，它既作为他的冲动而给出，又是为着那个尚未规定、没有方向的冲动而给出的。
不过，对于教养较高的心态及其道德性而言，还需要一种更为普遍的认识，即不仅要把一个民族的存在置于眼前，而且还要知道它就是那作为自然、世界与历史而出现的存在。

这与先前所指出的、实践原则在康德体系中那种被把握方式的偏侧性是同一回事：即它抽离了理论环节，因而是主观的。——人们可能会以为，亚里士多德的责备毋宁恰恰涉及的是相反的一面，即针对苏格拉底把德性变成知识、亦即道德原则成了某种理论性的东西这一点。——不过首先，亚里士多德所责备的并不是伦理之中的普遍者、亦即善被把握这件事；毋宁说，在进一步的追究中他发现对它的考察是必要的，只不过他把这与关于德性的研究区分开来。
雅可比在这里与此有所偏离，因为他拒斥这种善的形式与一套义务论，并在此转而诉诸心。——善现在乃是自我意识的内在目的，而它的存在是一种自在自为的存在；就此而言它属于理论的一面；但它就此而言是偏侧的，因为它是以普遍者的形式而与具体的观念相对地固定住的。
相反，它的内容乃是它所应当者，即那个作为主观目的而被设定的东西。
与这一面相对的另一面则是实在性，即真正属于理论的环节，因为它总是作为非理性者、作为自然，既作为外在的、身体的，又作为内在的感觉、冲动、习俗与习性而被发现。
对这一自然的知识反过来又取得了非理性的这种形式，因为它缺少关于这自然「应当如何」的概念，不在其中认识绝对的终极目的，不把它认识为这一终极目的单纯的实现与表述；——同样，善也仍然是无精神的，它并不超越定在的立场、亦即单纯努力的立场，除非它通过实在性的这一观点来补足自己。

en: It happens, however, in yet another sense, that Jacobi here places the heart over against the good in itself, the true in itself; he says on S. 37 that he does not know it, has only a distant presentiment of it; he declares that it arouses his indignation when one wants to force upon him the will that wills nothing, this empty nut of self-sufficiency and freedom in the absolutely indeterminate, as an equivalent for it.
This would then be that good in itself.

Jacobi declares himself still more solemnly in the fine passage which follows: "Yes, I am the atheist and the godless, who, disgusted with the will that wills nothing, wants to lie as Desdemona lied in her dying; wants to lie and to deceive as the Pylades who presented himself as Orestes; wants to murder as Timoleon; wants to break law and oath as Epameinondas, as Johann de Witt; wants to resolve on suicide as Otho; wants to rob temples as David, - yes, wants to pull out ears of corn on the sabbath, merely because I am hungry and the law was made for the sake of man, not man for the sake of the law ..."

With the holiest certainty which I have in myself, I know that the privilegium aggratiandi for such crimes against the pure letter of the absolutely general law of reason is the true right of majesty of man, the seal of his dignity, of his divine nature." - The absoluteness which self-consciousness knows in itself cannot be expressed more warmly and more nobly than it is here.
But why does this majesty which is in it, this dignity, this divine nature, appear here as opposed to reason?

Is it not otherwise everywhere the most explicit assertion of Jacobi that reason is the supernatural, the divine in man which reveals God? - But this divine is here set over against the law of reason, the letter of the law and, in the examples adduced, the laws of determinate content which make this determinate content into an absolute, - the determinate laws which absolutely forbid lying, deceiving, murdering, breaking law and oath, resolving on suicide, robbing the temples, breaking the sabbath. - I want, says Jacobi, to do such things, authorized by the majesty which is in man! - Does he not here express an absolute will which wills nothing, i.e. not a determinate law, not a determinate universal, - a self-sufficiency and freedom in the absolutely indeterminate?

The actions of Desdemona, of Pylades, Timoleon and so on are outwardly concrete realities, but their interior is the will, the inwardly concrete, which attains this loftiness and majesty only through this infinite power of abstraction from the determinate, and is self-sufficiency and freedom solely through that, in that it knows itself as the absolutely indeterminate, the universal, the good in itself, and makes itself the absolutely indeterminate, but at the same time precisely for that reason determines itself only out of itself and is concrete action. - However important it is that the will be recognized as this all-powerful, purely universal negativity against the determinate, it is just as important to recognize and acknowledge the will in its particularization, the rights, duties, laws; they make up the content of the ethical or moral sphere.

If Jacobi only appeals to the indeterminate side of the majesty of personality and only speaks of it from the certainty which he finds in himself, then it is on the one hand the very same ground and the result which a dialectic has that brings the limit of the determinate rights, duties, moral or religious commands to consciousness.
But on the other hand it is equally important that the recognition of these limits should not be left to the heart alone.

Jacobi's appeal, as noted before, does not go against the good in itself, i.e. not against the will which in this pure self-consciousness of its own essence has lifted up all determinacy; if it were to go against the determinate insight into the finitude of the determinate laws, rights and duties, then no exposition would be needed of where this would lead, - no more than a justification of this determinate insight itself, since that whose insight it is is itself something determinate, a right, a duty, a law.
zh: 然而雅可比在这里把心与自在的善、自在的真相对峙，又是出于另一种意思；他在 S. 37 处说他并不认识自在的善，对它只有一种遥远的预感；他宣称，当人们想把那个什么都不要的意志、那种在绝对无规定者中的自立与自由的空壳硬塞给他，来替代那自在的善时，他感到愤怒。
那么这就等于那个自在的善。

雅可比在接下来那段漂亮的文字中更为庄严地自白说：「是的，我就是那个无神论者与亵神者：他厌恶那个什么都不要的意志，他要像临死的苔丝狄蒙娜那样说谎；要像那位为俄瑞斯忒冒充的皮拉得斯那样说谎与欺骗；要像提摩勒翁那样杀人；要像埃帕米农达斯、像约翰·德·维特那样破坏法律与誓言；要像奥托那样决意自杀；要像大卫那样劫掠圣殿，——是的，还要在安息日拔取麦穗，哪怕只是因为我饿了，而法律是为人的缘故制定的，并不是人为法律的缘故……」
「以我内心所具有的最神圣的确信，我知道：就这类违背绝对普遍的理性法则之纯粹字面的罪行而言，privilegium aggratiandi（宽恕之权）正是人的真正尊严权，是其人格之尊严、其神性之本质的印记。」——自我意识在自身中所认识的那种绝对性，没有比这里说得更温厚、更高贵了。
但为什么这种就在其中的威严、这种尊严、这种神性，在这里竟与理性相对立起来？

难道不正是雅可比到处最明确地主张：理性就是人身上那超自然的、神圣的东西，它启示上帝吗？——但这里，这神圣的东西只是与理性法则、法则的字面以及（在所引的例子里）那些具有确定内容、并把这一确定内容变成绝对者的内容性法则相对立；——与那些绝对禁止说谎、欺骗、杀人、破坏法律与誓言、决意自杀、劫掠圣殿、破坏安息日的确定法则相对立。——雅可比说：我要做这种事，凭的是人身上那种威严的授权！——他在这里所表述的，难道不就是一个什么都不要的绝对意志，即不是一条确定的法则、不是一个确定的普遍者——一种在绝对无规定者中的自立与自由吗？

苔丝狄蒙娜、皮拉得斯、提摩勒翁等人的行为在外在上是具体的现实，但它们的内核是那意志、那内在的具体者；它只有凭着那种从规定者出发作抽象的无穷力量才达到这份崇高与威严，也唯有凭着这一点才是自立与自由——因为它自知为绝对无规定者、普遍者、自在的善，并使自己成为绝对无规定者；但也正因如此，它才只从自身出发规定自己，才是具体的行动。——那么，意志被认识为这种反对规定者的、纯粹普遍的否定性固然十分重要，同样重要的是在意志的特殊化中、在权利、义务与法则中认识并承认意志；它们构成伦理或道德范围的内容。
如果雅可比只是诉诸人格性之威严的那不确定的一面，并且只是从他自己在内心中找到的确信出发谈论它，那么一方面，这正是那种辩证法所具有的同一根据与结果——这种辩证法使那些确定的权利、义务、道德的或宗教的诫命之界限进入意识。
但另一方面同样重要的是：对这些界限的认识不应仅仅托付给心。
如前所述，雅可比的诉求并不针对自在的善，即并不针对那个在这种纯粹的自我意识中依其本质已扬弃了一切规定性的意志；如果它要针对的是对那些确定的法则、权利与义务之有限性的确定认识，那么既不需要说明这将导致什么，也不需要为这一确定的认识本身作辩护——因为那个被认识的东西本身就是一个确定者、一种权利、一项义务、一条法则。

en: But this appeal also cannot go absolutely against these determinations themselves.

If the dialectic does indeed present the limits of them and thereby recognizes their conditionality and finitude, their subjection to a higher, then just as much their sphere, in which they have a positive validity, must be acknowledged.

It is equally a demand upon philosophy to show this necessity of the ethical determinations and of their validity as well as the higher in which they are grounded, which precisely for that reason also has power and majesty over them. - Yes, one might even be inclined to reserve the consciousness of this majesty for the place of science or the most sacred of religion and to keep it far from a popular treatment in which appeals to the feeling and the inner certainty of the subject are permitted, if one considers how the romantics easily break in upon morality as well, how gladly men are inclined to act generously rather than legally, nobly rather than morally, and how, in allowing themselves to act against the letter of the law, they absolve themselves not so much from the letter as from the law. - Moreover that action which, out of divine majesty, takes leave of the law, the examples of which Jacobi appeals to, is likewise conditioned, conditioned through the particular nature of character, above all through situation and circumstances, - and through what circumstances? through entanglements of the highest misfortune, through the rarest extreme need into which rare individuals are placed.
It would be sad for freedom if it could only prove its majesty and give itself actuality in extraordinary cases of cruel disruption of the ethical and natural life and in extraordinary individuals.
The ancients, on the contrary, found the highest morality in the life of a well-ordered state.
Of such a life one could also say that therein man is made and valid rather for the sake of the law than the law for the sake of man.

The reverse of the well-known sentence quoted above contained a high truth, in that it meant the positive, i.e. merely statutory law; but the ethical law taken in general, it is truer to say that man is made for it; for if one wants once to separate and set against each other law and man, then only the individuality, the sensual purposes of desire, is left to man, and these can only be considered as means in relation to the law.
zh: 但这一诉求同样不能绝对地针对这些规定本身。
如果辩证法确实展示了它们的界限，并由此认识到它们的有条件性与有限性、它们对一个更高者的从属，那么同样必须承认它们拥有积极有效性的那个范围。

同样，向哲学提出的一个要求是：既展示伦理规定及其有效性的这一必然性，也展示它们所建立于其中的那个更高者——正因如此，它对它们也具有威力与威严。——是的，人们甚至可能倾向于把对这种威严的意识留给科学的场所或宗教中至为神圣的东西，把它挡在那种通俗的处理之外——在那种处理中，向感觉与主体的内在确信的诉求是被允许的——如果人们考察一下浪漫派何等轻易地也侵入伦理领域，人们何等乐于宁愿宽宏而不循法、宁愿高贵而不讲道德地行事，以及他们在允许自己违背法则的字面时，何等少地把自己从法则、而非仅仅从字面上解放出来。——此外，那种出于神性之威严而离弃法则的行为——雅可比所援引的正是它的例子——同样是有条件的，是受性格的特殊禀性所条件，尤其受处境与情势所条件；——而是什么样的情势呢？是最高不幸的纠葛，是罕见的极端困苦，罕见的人被置于其中。
如果自由只能在伦理与自然生活遭到残酷撕裂的非常情形中、只在非常的人身上证明自己的威严并获得现实，那么关于自由就实在可悲了。
相反，古人是在一个治理良好的国家的生活中找到了最高的伦理。
对于这样一种生活，人们也可以说：其中，人毋宁是为了法则的缘故而被造就、并且有效，而法则却不是因人的缘故。
上面所引那句通行之说的反面，本身包含着一个高尚的真理，因为它指的是实定的、亦即纯粹法规性的法则；但伦理的法则若从一般来把握，那么说「人是为它而被造就的」大概更真实；因为一旦人们要把法则与人如此分开并相对立，那么留给人的就只剩个别性、欲求的感性目的，而这些只有在与法则的关系中才能被看作手段。

en: We now go on further to the treatise 'On the Divine Things'.

It is however beyond doubt still so present in the memory of the public since its first appearance that it would be inappropriate to dwell on it longer. - The first part concerns the one-sidedness of the positive in religion if this is to remain in merely external attitude, whereby the relation of man is represented as spiritless.

Jacobi brings out here in a fine exposition the necessity of the subjective moment, that, as it is expressed on S. 292, the seeing does not proceed from the things which are seen, the hearing not from that which is heard, the self not from the other; as on the other side the seeing sees nothing by itself, the hearing alone hears nothing, the self finally does not come to itself, but we must learn our existence from an other, - that the spirit in man alone bears witness to a God.
zh: 我们现在再转向《论神圣之物》一书。
然而毫无疑问，自它首次问世以来，它在公众的记忆中仍然如此鲜明，以至于在此上停留过久是不合宜的。——第一部分涉及宗教中实证的偏侧性：如果它应当仅仅保持一种纯外在的态度，那么人与其上帝的关系就被设想为无精神的了。
雅可比在这里一段漂亮的阐述中强调了主观环节的必然性：正如 S. 292 处所表述的，看并不从被看的东西而来，听并不从被听的东西而来，自我并不从另一个者而来；反过来，看独自什么也看不到，听独自什么也听不到，自我最终也并不是自己来到自己这里，而是我们必须从另一个者那里得知我们的定在；——只有人身上的精神才为一个上帝作证。

en: The other part of this treatise concerns the philosophy of nature.

The fundamental idea of this philosophy is no longer one of the abstractions and one-sidednesses which have just been designated or which form the basis of the systems considered above, but the concrete, the spirit itself.

Here then it is no longer a matter of opposing to it the intuition of the spirit, nor of confining oneself to the demonstration of the contradiction which the nature of everything concrete can easily achieve in it.

It would be a vain and fruitless labour to want to unravel the misunderstandings which have arisen in the discussions about this; I will confine myself to two remarks. - First, it already follows from the repeatedly renewed attempts to find the philosophy of nature its scientific form that it is not yet satisfied with itself in this, just as none of the presentations following one another has exhausted the completeness of the content, but each has been broken off again before completion after an opening carried out more or less far.
Both circumstances can provide a polemic with ground for advantageous attacks.

If the scientific form has not won its determinate and secure method, then the relation of nature and spirit must retain a determination of immediacy which is merely exposed to a well-grounded dialectic.
This relation can moreover be clarified into truth only through its complete carrying-through, and it must put off all the imperfect relations in which it appears before the end.
zh: 这本书的另一部分涉及自然哲学。
这一哲学的基本观念不再是刚才所指出的那些抽象与偏侧之一，也不再是上面所考察的那些体系的基础，而是具体者、就是精神本身。
因此在这里要做的已不再是与它的精神直观相对抗，也不再只是满足于指出那种矛盾——按照一切具体者的本性，这种矛盾在它里面是容易做出来的。
想要理清在这方面已经发生的那些误解，将是徒劳而无成果的劳作；我只限于两点说明。——首先，从一再重新开始的、为自然哲学寻找其科学形式的尝试中就已经可以看出的，是它在这方面尚未使自己满意；正如接踵而来的那些表述没有一个穷尽了内容的完整，每每都在推进了一段或多或少之后、在完成之前又再度中断。
这两种情况都可以为论战提供有利进攻的立足点。
如果这种科学形式还没有赢得它那确定而稳妥的方法，那么自然与精神的关系就必定保持着一种直接性的规定，而这种规定是暴露在一种有根据的辩证法面前的。
此外，这一关系只有通过贯彻到底才能被澄清为真理，并且必须卸去在终局之前它所呈现的一切不完整的关系。

en: But as concerns secondly Jacobi's dialectic in this, it depends not so much on the content of his standpoint as on the persistent form in which he asserts this standpoint.
Only this form therefore I will try to describe more closely.
It is well known that it has the peculiarity of being opposed to development from concepts, to proofs and to method in thinking.

When they are put forward stripped of these forms of knowledge by which an idea is shown to be necessary, the positive ideas of Jacobi show themselves only with the value of assurances; feeling, presentiment, immediacy of consciousness, intellectual intuition, faith, - an irresistible certainty of the ideas are given as the grounds of their truth.

What now takes the dryness out of the presentation of assurances and of the mere appeal to such grounds is the noble mind, the deep disposition and the whole many-sided culture of the revered, love-filled individual.
Surrounded by this the ideas appear full of feeling, present often with deep clarity, always witty.
The witty is a kind of surrogate for methodically trained thinking and for the reason advancing in such thinking.

Raised above understanding, it has the idea for its soul; it grasps the antithesis in which it lies; but since it does not bring to consciousness either its abstract thought or the dialectical transition in concepts, it has only concrete representations, also sensible thoughts, for its material, and is a striving to reflect the higher therein.

This appearance of the higher in what is sensible and in representations, which is brought about by the power of the spirit in such material, is associated with its own mild charm, with which the dusk attracts us.

We meet therefore also in all the essays before us a wealth of witty turns and images through which the deep emerges in its clarity and naivety, - often quite simple contrasts which make noticeable a wealth of great meaning, single passages which are by themselves far-reaching gnomes.

The merit of such fortunate inspirations and ingenious inventions is not only not to be unrecognized, but we may allow ourselves the enjoyment of them in so far as they are there for that, to stir the thought and the spiritual through sense and representation.
In this enjoyment we must not let ourselves be disturbed if the effort of the witty to make its viewpoints clear is led into an exaggeration of them and of the consequences.
For it is its right to drive itself to the extreme, because the form and shape of the expression is only a means and the violence which appears in it likewise belongs only to the means.
zh: 但就其次雅可比在这里的辩证法而言，它所系于的与其说是他的立场的实质，不如说是他坚持这一立场时所持的那种恒久的形式。
因此我只想把这种形式更仔细地描述一下。
众所周知，它有一种独特的性质：与从概念出发的展开、与证明、与思维中的方法相对立。
当这些实证的观念被脱去那些藉以证明一个观念为必然性的认识形式而直接呈现出来时，雅可比的那些实证观念便只显出断言的价值；感觉、预感、意识的直接性、理智直观、信仰，——对观念的不可抗拒的确信，都被指定为它们真理的根据。
而使这种断言的呈现与对这类根据的单纯诉求不再干瘪的，是这位可敬而多情的个人的高贵精神、深挚情怀与全部多方面的教养。
在这层氛围的环绕之下，这些观念饱含感情地浮现出来，此刻常常带着深沉的清晰，始终机智灵动。
机智乃是一种经过方法训练的思维、以及在这种思维中推进着的理性的替代物。
机智高出于知性，它以观念为它的灵魂；它抓住观念所处的那一反题；但由于它既不把这一反题的抽象思想、也不把概念中的辩证过渡带入意识，它所拥有的材料便只有具体的表象、乃至通晓的念头，于是它成了一种努力，要在材料中把那个更高者反思出来。
这种在通晓的念头与表象中显现出来的更高者的假象——它是凭精神在这种材料中的力量产生出来的——总带着它自己那种柔和的魅力，就像黄昏吸引我们那样。
因此，在眼前所有的论文中我们都遇到丰富的机智转折与形象，深邃的东西借此在它的清晰与质朴中显现出来，——往往是极简单的对立，其中却显露出大义的丰盈；还有一些段落，单独立着便是包罗甚广的箴言。
这类幸运的灵机与巧妙的发明之功，不仅不应被忽视，而且我们不妨尽情享受它们——只要它们是为了这个目的而在那里的，即通过感觉与表象去激发思想与精神性的东西。
在这一享受中，如果机智者想要弄清自己的观点的努力导致了对这些观点及其后果的夸大，我们也不必为此而不快。
因为把自身推向极端乃是它的权利：表达的形式与姿态不过是手段，而其中显现出的生硬同样只属于手段。

en: Only then does this manner become more disturbing when it shows itself in the speculative, especially when it shows itself there polemically.

For as much as the wit of philosophy itself has only the speculative as its inner but hidden driving-spring, so much can the speculative, where it is to be speculative, become manifest only in the form of the concept.

If the dusk of the witty is therefore lovely because the light of the idea seems in it, then it loses this merit where the light of reason shines, and what is peculiar to it over against this is then only darkness.

Everything which is otherwise permitted to this manner, the disconnected, the leaps, the boldness of expression, the sharpness of understanding and its exaggeration and obstinacy, the use of sensible representation, the appeal to feeling and to sound common sense, becomes here unfitting to the subject. - The outer shape also of the essays which the present volume contains shows no methodical and doctrinal, but accidental intentions and occasions, of which the prefaces make mention, together with the statement of the interruptions undergone and of the also repeated alteration of the original intention in the course of time and labour, - circumstances which are given for the understanding of the shape of these writings, a statement which on this side also attests the character of accidental outpourings or of an intermediate kind which has more of a letter than of an essay.
zh: 只有当这种作风显现在思辨之中、尤其显现在其中的论战姿态上时，它才变得更为碍事。
因为哲学本身的机智越是只把思辨作为其内在的、却隐藏着的发条，思辨就越是在它应当是思辨的地方，只能以概念的形式显现。
如果机智的黄昏之所以可爱，是因为观念之光在其中闪烁，那么在理性之光照耀的地方它就失去了这一功德；而与理性相对，它那特有的一切此时便只剩黑暗。

通常人们容许这种作风的一切——不连贯、跳跃、表达的大胆、知性的尖锐及其夸张与固执、感性表象的运用、向感觉与健全常识的诉求——在这里都变得与对象不相称。——本卷所收诸篇的外在形态也显示出并非方法性的、教义性的，而是偶然的意图与机缘；各篇的序言都提到这些，同时也交代了所遭受的打断，以及原初意图在时间与工作进程中屡次发生的改变，——交代这些情势是为了理解这些著述的形态，而这一交代从这一方面也证明了它们具有偶然倾泻的特征，或属于一种比论著更接近书信的中间种类。

en: Yet with Jacobi the case is peculiar in that he has not only this accidental form and the witty in an unconcerned way as the manner of his mind, but that he holds positively and polemically to the standpoint of declaring speculative knowledge, comprehending recognition, to be impossible, - yes even for something worse than the impossible, since we find in him for example the statement that a God who were known would be no longer a God, that man is inscrutable to himself and to the essence of God, because otherwise a more-than-divine faculty would dwell in man, God would have to be invented by man, - and other things in this sense.

It will hardly be denied that it is the common work of Jacobi and Kant to have put an end to the former metaphysics not so much in respect of its content as of its manner of knowledge, and thereby to have grounded the necessity of a completely changed view of the logical.
Jacobi has thereby made a lasting epoch in the history of German philosophy and, since outside Germany philosophy has quite decayed and expired, in the history of philosophy in general.

In acknowledging this merit with respect to recognition one must stop; for the further point is that, as Kant fixed the negative result against the finite forms of knowledge, Jacobi fixed it against recognition as such.

He has refrained from going further and, instead of understanding, which was so to speak before the soul of recognition, has now made reason and spirit the soul of recognition, to bring it forth again out of reason and spirit, to baptize it again with this, after the water-baptism of understanding. - To the assurances of Jacobi with regard to recognition only assurances could be opposed, to his authorities other authorities, for example the authority of Christianity, which makes the recognition of God the highest demand, as the Delphic Apollo makes the knowledge of himself, namely the knowledge of the absolute essence of self-consciousness.
zh: 不过雅可比这里的情形是特殊的：他不仅以自己精神的方式、不加造作地拥有这种形式的偶然性与机智，而且他还积极地、论战地坚持这样一个立场：宣称思辨的知识、以概念把握的认识是不可能的，——甚至比不可能还要糟，因为我们在他那里读到这样的说法：一个若被知道了的上帝就不再是上帝；人对自己以及对上帝的本质都是不可解的，因为否则在人里面就住着一个超神的能力，上帝就得由人发明出来，——以及诸如此类的说法。
恐怕不难承认：给旧形而上学画上句号的，与其说是就其内容、毋宁说是就其认识方式而言，正是雅可比与康德的共同工作；由此也就奠定了一种全然改变了的逻辑观的必要性。
雅可比由此在德国哲学史上、并且——因为在德国之外哲学已完全败坏与消亡——在一般哲学史上造成了一个持久的纪元。
在承认这一在认识方面的功绩时必须就此打住；因为进一步的问题是：康德把否定性的成果针对有限的认识形式固定下来，雅可比则把它针对认识本身固定下来。

他克制着自己不再往前走；他没有让那个此前可以说是认识之灵魂的知性继续做灵魂，而是如今让理性与精神成为认识的灵魂，让认识从理性与精神中重新产生出来，在知性的水洗礼之后又以理性与精神重新施洗。——对于雅可比在认识问题上的那些断言，人们只能以断言来相对，以别的权威来相对他的权威，例如基督教的权威：它把对上帝的认识规定为最高的诉求，正如德尔斐的阿波罗把对自身的认识——即对自我意识的绝对本质的认识——规定为最高的诉求。

en: What matters in the matter has been indicated above.
It would be clumsy to want to proceed polemically and dialectically against the witty.
On the one hand it is already inclined to misunderstandings on its own side.
Since the character of accidentality dwells in its form as such, it is open to it to seize on this or another side of a philosophical system and to hold fast against it this or another viewpoint.

For as grounded as the dialectic against the Kantian system was acknowledged above, when it holds the dry understanding of its abstractions against the originally-synthetic or properly spiritual of the same, which is just as unspiritual in its connection with them, so conversely this could be made valid against those, and instead of showing the inadmissibility of the originally-synthetic by the insistence on abstraction, rather the untruth of abstraction could be shown by the assertion of the synthetic, or better, the truth of the latter derived from the untruth of the former. - But in so far as the witty knows its way, its apprehension and having of the truth, only as an immediate consciousness, and asserts in the subject matter the exclusion of the concept from itself, then the misunderstanding must befall it that it does not recognize itself, its own intuition, according to both form and content, in expressions and shapes which are different from its own, but which contain the same content, the same material results, yet have thinking and the concept for their soul.

So it is not difficult, for example already in the first definitions of Spinoza - in the concept of the causa sui for itself, in the definition of the same as one whose nature can only be comprehended as existing, in the definition of substance as one which is in itself and is comprehended out of itself, i.e. whose concept does not need the concept of another thing - to find something higher than merely the rigid being, the spiritless necessity.

Rather the pure concept of freedom, of self-determining thinking, of spirit is contained in it, as much as in the subject-object. - Only the causa sui would have to be represented, for example, not as arisen in the mechanical way, as has happened on S. 416 (Über die Lehre des Spinoza) as if it were permissible to the proposition that everything has its cause, in order to be able to include God under it, that at God another cause and also another effect were formally cut off and he himself was added to cause and effect, so that the concept of the causa sui would properly not be a thought in and for itself but a merely external accommodation.
zh: 事情的要害在上面已经暗示过了。
而想要以论战和辩证的方式去对付这种机智，则是不巧妙的。
一方面，它本身就已经易于引起误解。
由于就其形式本身而言它就带有偶然性的性质，所以它大可抓住一个哲学体系的这一面或那一面，并针对它固定住这个或那个观点。

因此，正如上面所承认的，辩证法把康德体系那些抽象的干瘪知性针对该体系的「原初—综合」者、亦即真正精神者提出来时是何等有根据——后者与前者的联系同样是无精神的——那么反过来，后者也可以针对前者被提出来：人们不是通过坚持抽象来显示「原初—综合」者的不合法性，而是通过主张综合来显示抽象的不真实，或者更好地说，从前者的不真实推出后者的真理。——然而，就这种机智只知道以直接意识的方式去把握和占有真理、并且在题旨上主张把概念从自己身上排除出去而言，一种误解就必然落到它身上：它无法在那些与自身不同的表述与形态中——无论就形式还是就内容——重新认出自己与自己的直观；那些表述与形态包含着同样的内容、同样的实质成果，却以思维与概念作为它们的灵魂。
因此并不难，例如就在斯宾诺莎最初的那些定义中——在「自因」这一概念本身中，在把自因定义为这样一种东西、其本性只能被理解为存在着者的定义中，在把实体定义为那种在自身之中、并从自身出发被理解者、亦即其概念并不需要另一事物的概念的定义中——找到某种比那僵硬的存在、那无精神的必然性更高的东西。

毋宁说，其中所包含的是自由、那种自我规定的思维、精神之纯粹概念，正如它包含在主体—客体中一样。——只是例如，自因并不应当被设想为以机械的方式产生出来，正如在 S. 416 (Über die Lehre des Spinoza) 处所发生的那样：仿佛那个「一切都有其原因」的命题是可以把上帝也囊括进去的，以至于在上帝那里另一种原因以及另一种作用被形式上地剪除了，而上帝自己也被加为原因与作用；结果，自因这一概念其实并不是自在自为的一个思想，而只是一种纯外在的迁就。

en: By the way, on the occasion of the concept of cause it may be mentioned that it can appear as an inconsistency with the aversion to concepts and conceptual determinations when we see Jacobi lay weight on the point that God should be thought of not as the ground but as the cause of the world.

One may let it pass as a popular licence or, in philosophizing, as a momentary expedient to make use of such relations for the determination of the nature of God or of his relation to the world; it may be that the one has a slight advantage over the other with regard to one side, but both are equally only determinations of understanding, relations of finitude (vgl. S. 413), and are in this way incapable of comprehending the concept of spirit.

The causa sui is also in this respect the more ingenious, because it contains the causal relation at once in its counter-stroke against itself and the lifting up of its finitude, - not that it is not there at all, but at the same time this movement of lifting itself up; just as also, if God is thought of as determining himself as ground, he must equally essentially be thought of as eternally lifting up such a relation. - Such determinations, still more the darker ones which are contained in mere prepositions, for example outside me, above me and so on, will hardly serve to remove misunderstandings; the result has rather shown that they rather call forth and increase them.
For the mere plain understanding which is first of all thereby expressed, and indeed in the prepositions in a more imperfect way, is contrary to the idea of the spirit which rules in the rest.

Since, however, the emphasis is laid upon them, as if the opposition which is meant were truly comprehended in them, they already give a title to attacks on their own account, - the more so since other passages must contradict such assertions of the one side of the opposition.
Often it is precisely that side which is quite close at hand and is even connected through which that which is to be asserted is corrected and lifted up.

So Jacobi does maintain entirely that it is the supernatural in man which reveals God (S. 424), the highest essence in him which bears witness of a highest one outside him, - the spirit in him alone bears witness of a God (S. 325); this majesty in man is also, as quoted above, called his divine nature. - Thus it is said of itself that God is just as little outside me, for what would the God-forsaken divine thing in me be? - not even the God, as Jacobi wittily calls the unconscious nature-God, - nor the Evil, for this divine thing in me is the holy witness of God.

With the idea of the spirit as this witness in me, one cannot also find the main proposition in the letter to Fichte to agree, which is expressed on S. 49: "God is and is outside me, a living, self-subsistent being, or I am God.
There is no third."

One will rather see this opposition as contradicting the whole remaining sense of Jacobi and in particular that which on S. 254 is expressed in a fine image with regard to Christianity and indicated as the manifest direction of the treatise 'On the Divine Things', to show in manifold ways that the purely religious idealist and the purely religious materialist only divide themselves into the two shells of the shell which contains the pearl of Christianity.

In the above either-or, "there is no third", the principium exclusi tertii is assumed and acknowledged, a principle of understanding of the former logic, which both in its remaining extent and especially after this highest maxim of the one-sidedness of understanding constituted precisely the law of knowledge of the former metaphysics - a law of knowledge whose explicit rejection is a main thought and, as mentioned above, a main merit of Jacobi.
zh: 顺便借「原因」这一概念一提：当我们看到雅可比着重主张上帝应当不是被思考为世界的根据、而是被思考为世界的原因时，这似乎与对概念与概念规定的那种厌恶相矛盾。
人们可以把动用这类关系来确定上帝的本性或上帝与世界的关系，看作一种通俗的许可，或者在哲学思考中看作一时权宜的补救；也许就某一方面而言这一种比那一种略占便宜；但两者同样都只是知性的规定、有限性的关系（vgl. S. 413），因而无法把握精神的概念。

在这一重意上，自因也是更精巧的，因为它同时包含着因果关系对自身的反冲以及对其有限性的扬弃，——并不是说它全然不在，而是同时包含着那种自我扬弃的运动；同样，即便上帝被思考为作为根据而规定自身，也必定同样本质地、作为永恒地被思考为扬弃这样一个关系。——这类规定，尤其是那些更晦暗的、包含在单纯介词之中的规定（例如「在我之外」「在我之上」等等），大概不足以消除误解；结果反而表明，它们更其会引发并增加误解。
因为那首先是借介词表达出来的、而且在介词中以一种更不完善的方式表达出来的单纯浅白，与在其余一切中居于支配地位的精神之观念是相抵触的。
然而既是在它们身上被着重强调，仿佛那所意指的对立真正被把握在其中，它们本身就已经为攻击提供了正当理由，——更何况其他段落还必定与这一方的主张相抵触。
往往正是那一面被完全地摆在近旁、甚至被联结起来，而那本应被主张的东西正是通过它而被纠正与扬弃的。

雅可比全然主张：启示上帝的，乃是人身上那超自然的东西，是他内里的至高本质，它为一个在他之外的至高者作证（S. 424），——只有他内里的精神才为一个上帝作证（S. 325）；如上文所引，人身上这种威严也被称作他的神性。——这样一来，那就等于自己明说了：上帝同样并不在我之外，因为在我之中那被上帝离弃的神圣的东西又是什么呢？——甚至不是那个上帝，即雅可比机智地称之为无意识的上帝之自然者，——也不是那恶，因为在我之中这神圣的东西乃是上帝的神圣见证者。
以精神（作为在我之中的这一见证者）的观念，人们也就无法认为致费希特的信中那条主张与之相符；那条主张在 S. 49 处是这样表述的：「上帝是并且是在我之外，是一个活生生的、自为存在着的本质，或者我就是上帝。
没有第三种。」
人们反而会认为，这一对立与雅可比其余全部的旨趣相抵触，尤其是与那在 S. 254 处就基督教以一个漂亮的形象表述出来、并且被指为《论神圣之物》一书明显方向的东西相抵触；他以多种多样的方式指出：宗教的纯粹理想主义者与宗教的纯粹唯物主义者，只不过是把这只盛着基督教之珍珠的贝壳分在了两片壳之间。
在上述那个「非此即彼」——「没有第三种」——之中，排中律（principio exclusi tertii）被设定并得到承认：这是旧逻辑的一个知性原则；它无论就其其余范围、还是特别就知性偏侧性的这条最高准则来说，恰恰构成了旧形而上学的认识法则——而明确地弃绝这一认识法则，正是雅可比的一个主要思想、如上文所说，也是他的一项主要功绩。

en: The mind and the fundamental intuition of Jacobi are so far removed from such determinations of the dry understanding that his use of them, notwithstanding, in order to determine the nature of God, could well have occasioned nothing but misunderstandings, if it was to pass for more serious and be taken more seriously than was compatible with the sense of the deep thinker and his other witty forms. - In the general preface of this volume and in the particular preface to the treatise 'On the Divine Things' Jacobi lets himself in on some such misunderstandings which have befallen him, among others also with regard to his Christianity.
We meet in these philosophical discussions at all many expressions about personality.

Jacobi says, for example, to Fichte in the letter to him (S. 46), that he would not hold him personally to be no atheist, no godless man, even if he has to call his doctrine atheist just like that of Spinoza; precisely such a testimony he gives of him and adduces the fine passage about him in which he calls to him: "Be blessed for me, great, yes holy Benedictus! however you may philosophize about the nature of the highest being and go astray in words: his truth was in your soul, and his love was your life" - This heartfelt and true homage concerns a noble, so misrecognized shadow; something foreign and other, however, lies in public assertions about the personal disposition and religion of a present-day individual. - Given the way in which Jacobi was just now represented as expressing his views on the highest ideas, it was natural that these ideas and their investigation should slide over onto the person; so I too, without any further futile attempt, will close this notice with the expression of the feeling which the majority of the readers of Jacobi's writings presumably share with me, that in the study of them they have conversed with a loving and noble mind and have been stimulated in manifold ways, deeply, instructively and meaningfully.
zh: 雅可比的精神与基本观照，离那种干瘪知性的规定如此之远，以至于他尽管如此、却仍动用这类规定来确定上帝的本性，大概只会引起误解——如果这种用法被视为比与这位深沉思想者的意味及其余那些机智的形式相容的程度更当真的话。——在这一卷的总序与《论神圣之物》一书的专门前言中，雅可比谈到了若干这样落到他身上的误解，其中也有关于他的基督教的。
总之，在这些哲学的商讨中我们遇到许多关于人格性的表述。

雅可比例如在致费希特的信中（S. 46）对他说：纵使他不得不把费希特的学说与斯宾诺莎的学说一样称为无神论的，他个人仍不会把他看作无神论者、看作亵神者；恰恰相反的见证他给了费希特，并援引了那段赞美他的话，在其中他呼唤道：「愿你受我祝福，伟大的、乃至至圣的 Benedictus！纵使你也曾对至高者的本性作哲学思考、并在言辞上走入歧途：他的真理曾在你的灵魂中，而他的爱就是你的生命。」——这一番饱含深情而真实的敬意，所指的是一个高贵的、如此被误解的影子；然而，对一个当代者的个人心态与宗教作出公开断言，其中却包含着某种异质的、别的东西。——鉴于前面所展示的雅可比表达其关于最高观念之看法的方式，这些观念及其探究滑向该人格是自然而然的；所以我也不想再做徒劳的尝试去调解那些误解，而要以表达这样一种感觉来结束这篇评述：雅可比著作的大多数读者大概与我一样都有这样的感觉——在研读这些著作时与一种慈爱而高贵的精神作了交谈，并受到多方面的、深沉的、富于教益与意味的启发。

en: What attaches to this of itself is the mention still to be made of the pleasant addition of 23 letters, in which we see Jacobi in his most characteristic shape, that of the loving, thoughtful and cheerful personality; they will therefore need no further recommendation with our readers.

I pick out from it only a few samples concerning a particularly remarkable friend of Jacobi, Hamann, who is brought near to us in it in an interesting way, and whose writings we may perhaps hope to see collected by Jacobi.

Jacobi writes to his brother in Freiburg on 5 September 1787 the following about him: "The enjoyment which I have in him cannot be described; for with extraordinary men, what constitutes their particular and proper impression is precisely what cannot be described or indicated.
It is wonderful in how high a degree he unites almost all extremes in himself.

That is why also from youth he was heartily weary of the principio contradictionis (and so much the more of the principio exclusi tertii just mentioned) as well as of that of the sufficient reason, and always only pursued the coincidentiae oppositorum.

"The coincidence" (Jacobi does not take it here as an empty abyss, as formlessness, chaos, entirely indeterminate, nothing as nothing, but rather as the highest liveliness of the spirit), "the formula of the resolution of some opposite things in him, I am still not able to find completely, but I nevertheless receive almost every day new light upon it, while I constantly feed on the freedom of his mind, which brings forth between him and me the most precious harmony.
He is as inclined as I am to let his humour run free and to follow the view of the moment ...
Buchholz said jokingly of Hamann that he was a perfect indifferentist, and I have not dropped this nickname.
The most diverse, most heterogeneous things, whatever is only beautiful, true and whole in its own way, has its own life, discloses abundance and virtuosity, he enjoys with equal delight.
Omnia divina, et humana omnia ...

Lavater's thirst for miracles is a bitter vexation to him and excites his mistrust as regards the saintliness of the man, whom, however, he sincerely loves and honours", and so on. - Could we not, after all, have the certainty that Jacobi, as he here portrays the mind of Hamann and finds himself in harmony with him, should equally find himself in harmony with a knowledge which is only a consciousness of coincidence and a knowledge of the ideas of personality, freedom and God, not in the category of incomprehensible mysteries and miracles?
zh: 与此自然相联、尚须一提的，是那令人愉快的附赠：23 封信，在其中我们看到雅可比最富于特色的形态——那慈爱、善思而开朗的人格；因此在我们的读者那里，它们无需再作任何推荐。
我只从中摘出几则关于雅可比的一位格外引人注目的朋友哈曼的样本；他在这些信中以一种有趣的方式使我们更接近他本人，而他的著作我们或许有希望看到由雅可比收集起来。
雅可比在 1787 年 9 月 5 日致其弗赖堡的兄弟的信中，就他这样写道：「我从与他相处中所获得的享受是无法描述的；因为在非常之人身上，造成他们独特而本真印象的，恰恰就是那无法描述、无法指明的东西。
他在何等高的程度上把几乎所有的极端统一于自身，真是不可思议。
因此他从年轻时起就由衷地厌恶矛盾律（principio contradictionis）——因之更加厌恶前面提到的排中律（principio exclusi tertii）——以及充足根据律，而始终只追求对立者的重合（coincidentiae oppositorum）。
「这种重合」（雅可比在这里并不把它把握为一个空洞的深渊、一种无形态、一个混沌、一个全然无规定者、即无物之为无物，而是把它把握为精神的最高活泼性），「即他内里若干对立之物之化解的公式，我还不能完全找到它；不过我几乎每天都从中得到新的光明，同时我不断地以他心灵的自由为食粮——正是这种自由在他与我之间产生了最宝贵的和谐。」
他和我一样，倾向于让自己的心绪自由驰骋，追随此刻的所见……
布赫霍尔茨曾开玩笑说哈曼是个十足的无差别主义者，而我没有放弃这个绰号。
最不同、最异质的那些东西——凡是在自己的方式上美好、真实而完整，具有自己的生命，显示出丰盈与精湛的东西——他都以同样的欢悦去享受。
「Omnia divina, et humana omnia」（神圣的一切，以及凡俗的一切）……
拉瓦特对奇迹的渴慕于他是一种苦涩的烦恼，并且使他对这个人的圣洁产生猜疑——不过他由衷地爱这个并尊敬这个人」，等等。——由此我们难道不能有把握地说：雅可比既然在这里这样描画哈曼的精神、并且与他和谐地相合，他也同样应当与这样一种认识和谐地相合——这种认识只是一种对重合的意识，以及对人格性、自由与上帝这些观念的知识，而并不处于不可理解的秘密与奇迹这一范畴之中吗？
